diagrams.source:
Application architecture: UI -> ViewModel -> use case -> repository -> local/remote data
System design: Mobile client -> APIs -> services -> databases / caches / queues / workers
diagrams.narration: In application architecture, the flow usually starts at the user interface, then moves through the ViewModel, a use case, and a repository to local or remote data sources. System design looks at a wider scope: the mobile client communicates with APIs, and the system also includes services, databases, caches, queues, and workers.

diagrams.source:
Client -> Service -> Cache
                    | miss
                    v
                 Database
                    |
                    +-> populate cache
diagrams.narration: The client sends a request to the service. The service checks the cache first. If the value is present, it can return it immediately. On a cache miss, the service reads the data from the database, stores it in the cache, and then returns it to the client.
